```{r description_of_purpose, eval=TRUE, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE, cache=FALSE}

# Chunk 4: Description of the purpose of this Rmd file

### This Rmd file is intended to take summary statistics from both the UKB
### and OFH analyses performed using the Logistic_Regressions.ipynb notebook,
### the Age_at_Diagnosis.ipynb notebook, and the SummaryOfLogisticRegressions.Rmd 
### file, and produce a summary report for the paper on health disparities 
### and equity in genomic research.

### Once the UK Biobank returns to normal operations, the summary statistics 
### from the UKB analyses will be used directly by exporting the bulk logistic 
### regression, NRI, DeLong statistical tests, feature importance, and other 
### summary tables, rather than needing to be fetched from the knitted 
### SummaryOfLogisticRegressions.Rmd file.



```


```{r fetch_UKB_summary_stats, eval=TRUE, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE, cache=FALSE}

# Chunk 5: Load in UKB summary statistics

if (!requireNamespace("rvest", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("rvest")
}

if (!requireNamespace("purrr", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("purrr")
}

if (!requireNamespace("readr", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("readr")
}

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(stringr)
library(ggplot2)
library(rvest)
library(purrr)
library(readr)

#################################################################################################################
# Step 0 - automatically extract tables from the knitted Rmd html, or fetch tables from exported .tsvs or .csvs #
#################################################################################################################

# Check the user-specified source is valid
valid_UKB_summary_table_sources <- c("RMarkdown_HTML", "Exported_tables")

if (!UKB_summary_table_source %in% valid_UKB_summary_table_sources) {
  stop(
    "Invalid value for UKB_summary_table_source. Please choose either 'RMarkdown_HTML' or 'Exported_tables'."
  )
}

# Helper functions

predictor_name_map <- c(
  ContimultiethnicGRS267 = "GRS269-Multi",
  ContiAfricanGRS246 = "GRS269-AFR",
  ContiORadjustedGRS = "GRS269-ORadj",
  WangAfricanGRS444 = "GRS451-AFR",
  BARCODE1GRS129 = "BARCODE1",
  GenomicsPLC_PRS = "GenomicsLtd",
  SeibertGRS52 = "PHS54",
  PagadalaGRS285 = "PHS290",
  SchumacherGRS145 = "GRS147",
  ContiMultiethnicGRS = "GRS269-Multi",
  ContiEURGRS = "GRS269-EUR",
  ContiAFRGRS = "GRS269-AFR",
  ContiEASGRS = "GRS269-EAS",
  ContiHISGRS = "GRS269-HIS",
  WangMultiethnicGRS = "GRS451-Multi",
  WangEURGRS = "GRS451-EUR",
  WangAFRGRS = "GRS451-AFR",
  WangEASGRS = "GRS451-EAS",
  WangHISGRS = "GRS451-HIS"
)

rename_model_terms <- function(values) {
  vapply(values, function(value) {
    if (is.na(value)) {
      return(NA_character_)
    }

    terms <- stringr::str_split(value, stringr::fixed(" + "))[[1]]
    renamed_terms <- unname(predictor_name_map[terms])
    renamed_terms[is.na(renamed_terms)] <- terms[is.na(renamed_terms)]

    paste(renamed_terms, collapse = " + ")
  }, character(1))
}

process_summary_table <- function(df) {
  # Split ROC AUC column if present, but only if split columns are not already present
  roc_split_cols <- c("ROC_AUC", "ROC_AUC_CI_Lower", "ROC_AUC_CI_Upper")
  
  if ("ROC_AUC_CI_95_4dp" %in% names(df) &&
      !any(roc_split_cols %in% names(df))) {
    
    df <- df %>%
      extract(
        col = ROC_AUC_CI_95_4dp,
        into = roc_split_cols,
        regex = "([0-9.]+)\\s*\\[\\s*([0-9.]+)\\s*-\\s*([0-9.]+)\\s*\\]",
        remove = FALSE
      )
  }
  
  # Split OR per 1SD column if present, but only if split columns are not already present
  or_split_cols <- c("OR_per_1SD", "OR_per_1SD_CI_Lower", "OR_per_1SD_CI_Upper")
  
  if ("OR_per_1SD_CI_95" %in% names(df) &&
      !any(or_split_cols %in% names(df))) {
    
    df <- df %>%
      extract(
        col = OR_per_1SD_CI_95,
        into = or_split_cols,
        regex = "([0-9.]+)\\s*\\[\\s*([0-9.]+)\\s*-\\s*([0-9.]+)\\s*\\]",
        remove = FALSE
      )
  }
  
  # Convert split columns to numeric, but only if they exist
  numeric_cols <- c(
    "ROC_AUC", "ROC_AUC_CI_Lower", "ROC_AUC_CI_Upper",
    "OR_per_1SD", "OR_per_1SD_CI_Lower", "OR_per_1SD_CI_Upper",
    "AUC_A", "AUC_B", "p_value", "p_value_BH"
  )
  
  df <- df %>%
    mutate(across(any_of(numeric_cols), as.numeric))
  
  # Rename predictors and model terms using the same component-level map.
  df <- df %>%
    mutate(
      across(
        any_of(c("Predictor", "Model_A", "Model_B", "Model")),
        rename_model_terms
      )
    )
  
  # Clean family-history labels in covariate and model columns.
  df <- df %>%
    mutate(
      across(
        any_of(c("Covariates", "Model_A", "Model_B", "Model")),
        ~ str_replace_all(.x, "FH_PrCa_BrCa", "FHx")
      )
    )

  df <- df %>%
    mutate(
      across(
        any_of(c("Covariates", "Model_A", "Model_B", "Model")),
        ~ str_replace_all(.x, "FHx_PrCa_BrCa", "FHx")
      )
    )
  
  return(df)
}

has_cols <- function(df, cols) {
  all(cols %in% names(df))
}

merge_table_group <- function(tbl_list) {
  if (length(tbl_list) == 0) {
    return(tibble())
  }
  
  bind_rows(tbl_list, .id = "source_table")
}

safe_distinct <- function(df, cols) {
  if (nrow(df) == 0) {
    return(df)
  }
  
  available_cols <- cols[cols %in% names(df)]
  
  if (length(available_cols) == 0) {
    return(df)
  }
  
  df %>%
    distinct(across(all_of(available_cols)), .keep_all = TRUE)
}

keep_by_filename <- function(tbl_list, pattern, ignore_case = TRUE) {
  tbl_list[
    str_detect(
      names(tbl_list),
      regex(pattern, ignore_case = ignore_case)
    )
  ]
}

get_exported_group <- function(tbl_list, user_file, pattern) {
  
  if (!is.null(user_file)) {
    
    if (!user_file %in% names(tbl_list)) {
      stop("Specified file not found in exported tables: ", user_file)
    }
    
    return(tbl_list[user_file])
    
  } else {
    
    return(keep_by_filename(tbl_list, pattern))
  }
}

#######################################################################
#======= Step 1 - Read summary tables from the selected source =======#
#######################################################################

if (UKB_summary_table_source == "Exported_tables") {
  
  table_files <- list.files(
    path = UKB_exported_tables_directory,
    pattern = "\\.(tsv|csv)$",
    full.names = TRUE,
    ignore.case = TRUE
  )
  
  if (length(table_files) == 0) {
    stop("No .tsv or .csv files found in: ", UKB_exported_tables_directory)
  }
  
  summary_tables <- table_files %>%
    map(~ read_delim(
      .x,
      delim = ifelse(
        str_detect(.x, regex("\\.tsv$", ignore_case = TRUE)),
        "\t",
        ","
      ),
      col_types = cols(.default = "c")
    )) %>%
    set_names(basename(table_files))
  
  print(paste(
    "From the exported tables directory:",
    UKB_exported_tables_directory,
    ",",
    length(summary_tables),
    "tables were identified"
  ))
  
} else if (UKB_summary_table_source == "RMarkdown_HTML") {
  
  if (!file.exists(UKB_html_file_path)) {
    stop("The specified HTML file does not exist: ", UKB_html_file_path)
  }

  html_file <- read_html(UKB_html_file_path)
  
  summary_tables <- html_file %>%
    html_elements("table") %>%
    html_table(trim = TRUE, convert = FALSE) %>%
    set_names(paste0("summary_table_", seq_along(.)))
  
  print(paste(
    "From the Rmarkdown summary document,",
    length(summary_tables),
    "tables were identified"
  ))
}

##################################################################
#======= Step 2 - Apply cleaning/processing to all tables =======#
##################################################################

summary_tables_processed <- summary_tables %>%
  imap(~ process_summary_table(.x))

############################################################
# Step 3 - Group tables into common final summary objects  #
############################################################

if (UKB_summary_table_source == "Exported_tables") {
  
  symptomatic_triage_tables <- get_exported_group(
    summary_tables_processed,
    symptomatic_triage_table,
    "symptomatic_triage"
  )
  
  asymptomatic_screening_tables <- get_exported_group(
    summary_tables_processed,
    asymptomatic_screening_table,
    "asymptomatic_screening"
  )
  
  paired_DeLong_test_tables <- get_exported_group(
    summary_tables_processed,
    paired_DeLong_test_table,
    "paired_DeLong_test"
  )
  
  unpaired_DeLong_test_tables <- get_exported_group(
    summary_tables_processed,
    unpaired_DeLong_test_table,
    "unpaired_DeLong_test"
  )
  
  odds_ratio_tables <- get_exported_group(
    summary_tables_processed,
    odds_ratio_table,
    "odds_ratio"
  )
  
  NRI_tables <- get_exported_group(
    summary_tables_processed,
    NRI_table,
    "NRI"
  )
  
  statistical_feature_importance_tables <- get_exported_group(
    summary_tables_processed,
    statistical_feature_importance_table,
    "statistical_feature_importance"
  )
  
  machine_learning_feature_importance_tables <- get_exported_group(
    summary_tables_processed,
    machine_learning_feature_importance_table,
    "machine_learning_feature_importance"
  )
  
} else if (UKB_summary_table_source == "RMarkdown_HTML") {
  
  if (length(summary_tables_processed) < 101) {
    stop(
      "Expected at least 101 tables in the HTML source because tables 98-101 are assumed to be symptomatic triage tables. Only ",
      length(summary_tables_processed),
      " tables were found."
    )
  }
  
  symptomatic_triage_tables <- summary_tables_processed[98:101]
  
  tables_for_classification <- summary_tables_processed[-c(98:101)]
  
  asymptomatic_screening_tables <- tables_for_classification %>%
    keep(~ has_cols(.x, c("ROC_AUC_CI_95_4dp", "OR_per_1SD_CI_95")))
  
  paired_DeLong_test_tables <- tables_for_classification %>%
    keep(~ has_cols(.x, c("Model_A", "Model_B")))
  
  unpaired_DeLong_test_tables <- tables_for_classification %>%
    keep(~ has_cols(.x, c("Population_A", "Population_B")))
  
  odds_ratio_tables <- tables_for_classification %>%
    keep(~ has_cols(.x, "Bin"))
  
  NRI_tables <- tables_for_classification %>%
    keep(~ has_cols(.x, "NRI"))
  
  statistical_feature_importance_tables <- tables_for_classification %>%
    keep(~ has_cols(.x, "Full_ROC_AUC_4dp"))
  
  machine_learning_feature_importance_tables <- tables_for_classification %>%
    keep(~ has_cols(.x, "Age_Pct_Importance_1dp"))
}

############################################
# Step 4 - Create common final data frames #
############################################

symptomatic_triage_summary <- merge_table_group(symptomatic_triage_tables)

asymptomatic_screening_summary <- merge_table_group(asymptomatic_screening_tables) %>%
  safe_distinct(c("Outcome", "Population", "Predictor", "Covariates", "ROC_AUC"))

asymptomatic_screening_outcomes <- asymptomatic_screening_summary %>%
  dplyr::distinct(source_table, Outcome) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    source_table_number = as.integer(stringr::str_extract(source_table, "\\d+$")),
    paired_source_table = paste0("summary_table_", source_table_number + 1L),
    unpaired_source_table = paste0("summary_table_", source_table_number + 2L)
  )

paired_DeLong_test_summary <- merge_table_group(paired_DeLong_test_tables) %>%
  safe_distinct(c("Model_A", "Model_B", "Population", "AUC_A", "AUC_B", "p_value", "N_usable")) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    asymptomatic_screening_outcomes %>%
      dplyr::select(source_table = paired_source_table, Outcome),
    by = "source_table"
  ) %>% dplyr::mutate(
    Delta_AUC = AUC_B - AUC_A       ## Ensure delta AUC has the right sign (AUC_B - AUC_A, not AUC_A - AUC_B)
  ) %>% dplyr::filter(              ## filter to statistical tests relevant for this paper
      Population == "White" | Population == "Black",
      Outcome == "PrCa_2yrs" | Outcome == "PrCa_5yrs" | Outcome == "PrCa_10yrs" | Outcome == "PrCa_actionable_2yrs" | Outcome == "PrCa_actionable_5yrs" | Outcome == "PrCa_actionable_10yrs",
      Model_A != "GRS147" & Model_A != "GRS147 + Age" & Model_A != "GRS147 + FHx" & Model_A != "GRS147 + Age + FHx" & Model_A != "GRS269-ORadj" & Model_A != "GRS269-ORadj + Age" & Model_A != "GRS269-ORadj + FHx" & Model_A != "GRS269-ORadj + Age + FHx" & Model_A != "NA" & Model_A != "PHS290" & Model_A != "PHS290 + Age" & Model_A != "PHS290 + FHx" & Model_A != "PHS290 + Age + FHx" & Model_A != "PHS54" & Model_A != "PHS54 + Age" & Model_A != "PHS54 + FHx" & Model_A != "PHS54 + Age + FHx",
      Model_B != "GRS147" & Model_B != "GRS147 + Age" & Model_B != "GRS147 + FHx" & Model_B != "GRS147 + Age + FHx" & Model_B != "GRS269-ORadj" & Model_B != "GRS269-ORadj + Age" & Model_B != "GRS269-ORadj + FHx" & Model_B != "GRS269-ORadj + Age + FHx" & Model_B != "NA" & Model_B != "PHS290" & Model_B != "PHS290 + Age" & Model_B != "PHS290 + FHx" & Model_B != "PHS290 + Age + FHx" & Model_B != "PHS54" & Model_B != "PHS54 + Age" & Model_B != "PHS54 + FHx" & Model_B != "PHS54 + Age + FHx"
  ) %>% dplyr::mutate(                            ## readjust BH p values so that only tests relevant for this paper are considered
    p_value_BH = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH")
  ) %>% dplyr::select(
    Population, Outcome, Model_A, Model_B, AUC_A, AUC_B, Delta_AUC, p_value, p_value_BH, N_usable, Test
  )
  

unpaired_DeLong_test_summary <- merge_table_group(unpaired_DeLong_test_tables) %>%
  safe_distinct(c("Population_A", "Population_B", "Model", "AUC_A", "AUC_B", "p_value", "N_A", "N_B")) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(
    asymptomatic_screening_outcomes %>%
      dplyr::select(source_table = unpaired_source_table, Outcome),
    by = "source_table"
  ) %>% dplyr::mutate(
    Delta_AUC = AUC_B - AUC_A       ## Ensure delta AUC has the right sign (AUC_B - AUC_A, not AUC_A - AUC_B)
  ) %>% dplyr::filter(              ## filter to statistical tests relevant for this paper
      Population_A == "White" & Population_B == "Black",
      Outcome == "PrCa_2yrs" | Outcome == "PrCa_5yrs" | Outcome == "PrCa_10yrs" | Outcome == "PrCa_actionable_2yrs" | Outcome == "PrCa_actionable_5yrs" | Outcome == "PrCa_actionable_10yrs",
      Model != "GRS147" & Model != "GRS147 + Age" & Model != "GRS147 + FHx" & Model != "GRS147 + Age + FHx" & Model != "GRS269-ORadj" & Model != "GRS269-ORadj + Age" & Model != "GRS269-ORadj + FHx" & Model != "GRS269-ORadj + Age + FHx" & Model != "NA" & Model != "PHS290" & Model != "PHS290 + Age" & Model != "PHS290 + FHx" & Model != "PHS290 + Age + FHx" & Model != "PHS54" & Model != "PHS54 + Age" & Model != "PHS54 + FHx" & Model != "PHS54 + Age + FHx"
  ) %>% dplyr::mutate(                             ## Again, readjust BH p values so that only tests relevant for this paper are considered
    p_value_BH = p.adjust(p_value, method = "BH")
  ) %>% dplyr::select(
    Population_A, Population_B, Outcome, Model, AUC_A, AUC_B, Delta_AUC, p_value, N_A, N_B, p_value_BH, Test
  )

odds_ratio_summary <- merge_table_group(odds_ratio_tables) %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    "White men, Age" = "White men, Age alone",
    "Black men, Age" = "Black men, Age alone"
  )

NRI_summary <- merge_table_group(NRI_tables)

statistical_feature_importance_summary <- merge_table_group(
  statistical_feature_importance_tables
)

machine_learning_feature_importance_summary <- merge_table_group(
  machine_learning_feature_importance_tables
)

```

```{r fetch_OFH_summary_stats, eval=TRUE, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE, cache=FALSE}

# Chunk 6: Load in OFH summary statistics

######################################################
# Step 0 - find tables and load them as R dataframes #
######################################################

asymptomatic_screening_table_OFH_df <- read.csv(file.path(
                                                  OFH_exported_tables_directory, 
                                                  asymptomatic_screening_table_OFH
                                                ), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

age_at_diagnosis_table_OFH_df <- read.csv(file.path(
                                              OFH_exported_tables_directory, 
                                              age_at_diagnosis_table_OFH
                                            ), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

unpaired_DeLong_test_table_OFH_df <- read.csv(file.path(
                                                      OFH_exported_tables_directory, 
                                                      unpaired_DeLong_test_table_OFH
                                                    ), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

screening_date_DeLong_test_table_OFH_df <- read.csv(file.path(
                                                      OFH_exported_tables_directory, 
                                                      screening_date_DeLong_test_table_OFH
                                                    ), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)


## Apply same processing to these OFH dataframes as that done for UKB dataframes

asymptomatic_screening_OFH <- process_summary_table(asymptomatic_screening_table_OFH_df)
age_at_diagnosis_OFH <- process_summary_table(age_at_diagnosis_table_OFH_df)
unpaired_DeLong_test_OFH <- process_summary_table(unpaired_DeLong_test_table_OFH_df)
screening_date_DeLong_test_OFH <- process_summary_table(screening_date_DeLong_test_table_OFH_df)

## Ensure that shared columns between the UKB and OFH
## asymptomatic_screening_table are the same name

UKB_OFH_shared_columns <- intersect(
  names(asymptomatic_screening_summary),
  names(asymptomatic_screening_OFH)
)

if (!setequal(UKB_OFH_shared_columns, shared_column_names)) {
  stop(
    "The shared columns between the UKB and OFH asymptomatic screening summary tables do not match the expected names. ",
    "Please check the column names in both tables. The expected shared columns are: ",
    paste(shared_column_names, collapse = ", "), ". The actual shared columns are: ",
    paste(UKB_OFH_shared_columns, collapse = ", ")
  )
}
```

```{r setup_plotting_functions, eval=TRUE, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE, cache=FALSE}

# Chunk 7: Set up plotting and reporting functions

## Set colour palette for plots
study_palette <- c(
  "#00c896", "#e60000", "#ffc62c", "#6ab3e7", "#ff7f41", "#9569be", "#007d69", "#702081", "#e78699", 
  "#00a87e", "#b46a55", "#93272c", "#f9423a", "#fc4c02", "#f3d54e", "#250e62", "#022020", "#003c3c",  
  "#00dca5", "#f4c3cd", "#898b8d"
)

# Setup "create_forest_plot" function to generate forest plots for the summary statistics

create_forest_plot <- function(data = NULL,
                               outcome = NULL,
                               screening_date = NULL,
                               populations = c("White", "Black", "EUR", "AFR"),
                               predictors = NULL,
                               covariates = NULL,
                               metric = NULL,
                               title = TRUE,
                               grouping = "model",     # Can be set to "model" or "screening_date"
                               key = TRUE,
                               suppress_warnings = FALSE,
                               point_size = 2.5) {

## Warning messages to guide users (note: do not stop, just print warning messages)

if (is.null(data)) {
  print("Warning: Please provide a data frame for the 'data' argument. This should be a summary statistics data frame containing the relevant columns for the specified outcome, screening date, populations, predictors, covariates, and metric.")
  return(NULL)
}

is_ofh_data <- "Screening_Date" %in% names(data)

if (!grouping %in% c("model", "screening_date")) {
  stop(paste0("Error: grouping must be set to 'model' or 'screening_date'"))
}

if (grouping == "screening_date" & !is_ofh_data) {
  stop(paste0("Error: grouping cannot be set to 'screening_date' if 'Screening_Date' is not found in the table column names"))
}

if (is_ofh_data) {
  if (is.null(predictors)) {
    predictors <- c("age_asd", "GRS269-AFR", "GRS269-EUR", "GRS269-Multi", "GRS451-AFR", "GRS451-EUR", "GRS451-Multi")
  }
  if (is.null(covariates)) {
    covariates <- c("None", "age_asd", "FHx_PrCa_BrCa", "age_asd + FHx_PrCa_BrCa")
  }

  include_age_only <- "age_asd" %in% predictors

  if (grouping == "model") {
    if (!is.null(outcome) & !is.null(screening_date) & !is.null(metric)) {
      if (title) {
        print(paste0("Creating forest plot for outcome '", outcome, "' at screening date '", screening_date, "' using metric '", metric, "'"))
      }
    } else {
      print("Warning: Please specify an outcome, screening date, and metric to create the forest plot.")
    }
  } else if (grouping == "screening_date") {
    if (!is.null(outcome) & !is.null(metric)) {
      if (title) {
        print(paste0("Creating forest plot for outcome '", outcome, "' grouped by screening date using metric '", metric, "'"))
      }
    } else {
      print("Warning: Please specify an outcome and metric to create the forest plot.")
    }
  }

  if (grouping == "model" && !is.null(screening_date) && !screening_date %in% unique(data$Screening_Date)) {
    if (!suppress_warnings) {
      print(paste0("Warning: Screening date '", screening_date, "' not found in the data. Please check the available screening dates. These are typically: 'artificial_screening_date', 'date40', 'date50', 'date55', 'date60', 'date65'"))
    }
  }

  if (!is.null(outcome) && !outcome %in% unique(data$Outcome)) {
    if (!suppress_warnings) {
      print(paste0("Warning: Outcome '", outcome, "' not found in the data. Please check the available outcomes. These are typically: 'PrCa_post_assessment', 'PrCa_2yrs', 'PrCa_5yrs', 'PrCa_10yrs'"))
    }
  }

  if (!all(populations %in% unique(data$Population))) {
    unidentified_populations <- populations[!populations %in% unique(data$Population)]
    if (!suppress_warnings) {
      print(paste0("Warning: One or more populations not found in the data: ", paste(unidentified_populations, collapse = ", "), ". Please check the available populations. These are typically: 'White', 'Black', 'EUR', 'AFR'"))
    }
  }

  if (!all(predictors %in% unique(data$Predictor))) {
    if (!suppress_warnings) {
      print(paste0("Warning: One or more predictors not found in the data. Please check the available predictors. These are typically: 'age_asd', 'GRS269-AFR', 'GRS269-EUR', 'GRS269-Multi', 'GRS451-AFR', 'GRS451-EUR', 'GRS451-Multi'"))
    }
  }

  if (!all(covariates %in% unique(data$Covariates))) {
    if (!suppress_warnings) {
      print(paste0("Warning: One or more covariates not found in the data. Please check the available covariates. These are typically: 'None', 'age_asd', 'FHx_PrCa_BrCa', 'age_asd + FHx_PrCa_BrCa'"))
    }
  }

  if (!is.null(metric) && !metric %in% c("ROC_AUC", "OR_per_1SD_global", "OR_per_1SD_subpopulation")) {
    if (!suppress_warnings) {
      print(paste0("Warning: Metric '", metric, "' not found in the data. Please check the available metrics. These are typically: 'ROC_AUC', 'OR_per_1SD_global', 'OR_per_1SD_subpopulation'"))
    }
  }





if (grouping == "model") {

  base_forestplot <- data %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      Population %in% populations,
      Predictor %in% predictors,
      (Covariates %in% covariates) |
        (include_age_only & Predictor == "age_asd" & Covariates == "None"),
      Outcome == outcome,
      Screening_Date == screening_date
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Population = factor(Population, levels = rev(populations)),
      Plot_Group = paste(Predictor, Covariates, sep = " | ")
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Covariate_Count = dplyr::if_else(
        Covariates == "None",
        0L,
        stringr::str_count(Covariates, "\\+") + 1L
      ),
      Group_Order = dplyr::case_when(
        Predictor == "age_asd" & Covariates == "None" ~ 1,
        stringr::str_detect(Predictor, "GRS269-Multi|ContimultiethnicGRS267|ContiMultiethnicGRS") ~ 2,
        TRUE ~ 3
      )
    )

  group_levels <- base_forestplot %>%
    dplyr::distinct(Plot_Group, Predictor, Covariates, Group_Order, Covariate_Count) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(Group_Order, Predictor, Covariate_Count, Covariates) %>%
    dplyr::pull(Plot_Group)

  group_palette <- setNames(study_palette[seq_along(group_levels)], group_levels)

} else if (grouping == "screening_date") {

  base_forestplot <- data %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      Population %in% populations,
      Predictor %in% predictors,
      (Covariates %in% covariates) |
        (include_age_only & Predictor == "age_asd" & Covariates == "None"),
      Outcome == outcome
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Population = factor(Population, levels = rev(populations)),
      Plot_Group = dplyr::case_when(
        Screening_Date == "artificial_screening_date" ~ "31/12/2013",
        Screening_Date == "date40" ~ "Age 40",
        Screening_Date == "date50" ~ "Age 50",
        Screening_Date == "date55" ~ "Age 55",
        Screening_Date == "date60" ~ "Age 60",
        Screening_Date == "date65" ~ "Age 65",
        TRUE ~ Screening_Date
      )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Covariate_Count = dplyr::if_else(
        Covariates == "None",
        0L,
        stringr::str_count(Covariates, "\\+") + 1L
      ),
      Group_Order = dplyr::case_when(
        Screening_Date == "artificial_screening_date" ~ 1,
        Screening_Date == "date40" ~ 2,
        Screening_Date == "date50" ~ 3,
        Screening_Date == "date55" ~ 4,
        Screening_Date == "date60" ~ 5,
        Screening_Date == "date65" ~ 6,
        TRUE ~ 99
      )
    )

    group_levels <- base_forestplot %>%
      dplyr::distinct(Plot_Group, Group_Order) %>%
      dplyr::arrange(Group_Order, Plot_Group)  %>%
      dplyr::pull(Plot_Group)

    group_palette <- setNames(study_palette[seq_along(group_levels)], group_levels)
}

  forestplot <- base_forestplot %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      !is.na(.data[[metric]]),
      !is.na(.data[[paste0(metric, "_CI_Lower")]]),
      !is.na(.data[[paste0(metric, "_CI_Upper")]])
    ) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(Group_Order, Predictor, Covariate_Count, Covariates) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Plot_Group = factor(Plot_Group, levels = group_levels)
    )

  dodge_pos <- position_dodge(width = 0.6, reverse = TRUE)

  plot_limits <- if (metric == "ROC_AUC") {
      c(0.5, 1.0)
    } else if (metric %in% c("OR_per_1SD_global", "OR_per_1SD_subpopulation")) {
      c(1, 8)
    } else {
      NULL
    }

  outcome_label <- dplyr::case_when(
    outcome == "PrCa_2yrs" ~ "2-year",
    outcome == "PrCa_5yrs" ~ "5-year",
    outcome == "PrCa_10yrs" ~ "10-year",
    outcome == "PrCa_post_assessment" ~ "Post-assessment",
    TRUE ~ outcome
  )

  metric_label <- dplyr::case_when(
    metric == "ROC_AUC" ~ "ROC AUC",
    metric == "OR_per_1SD_global" ~ "OR per 1SD (Global)",
    metric == "OR_per_1SD_subpopulation" ~ "OR per 1SD (Subpopulation)",
    TRUE ~ metric
  )

  metric_axis_label <- paste0(outcome_label, " ", metric_label, " [95% CI]")
  
  plot_obj <- ggplot(
    forestplot,
    aes(x = Population, y = .data[[metric]], color = Plot_Group)
  ) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = ifelse(metric == "ROC_AUC", 0.5, 1), linetype = "dashed", color = "#898b8d") +
    geom_errorbar(
      aes(ymin = .data[[paste0(metric, "_CI_Lower")]], ymax = .data[[paste0(metric, "_CI_Upper")]]),
      position = dodge_pos,
      width = 0.2,
      linewidth = 0.5
    ) +
    geom_point(
      position = dodge_pos,
      size = point_size
    ) +
    coord_flip(ylim = plot_limits) +
    labs(
      title = if (isTRUE(title)) {
        if (grouping == "model") {
          paste0("Forest plot for outcome '", outcome, "' at screening date '", screening_date, "'")
        } else {
          paste0("Forest plot for outcome '", outcome, "' grouped by screening date")
        }
      } else {
        NULL
      },
      x = "Population",
      y = metric_axis_label,
      color = ifelse(grouping == "model", "Model", "Screening date")
    ) +
    scale_color_manual(values = group_palette) +
    guides(color = guide_legend(reverse = FALSE)) +
    theme_minimal()

  if (!isTRUE(key)) {
    plot_obj <- plot_obj + theme(legend.position = "none")
  }

  return(plot_obj)
} else {
  if (is.null(predictors)) {
    predictors <- c("Age", "GRS269-AFR", "GRS269-EUR", "GRS269-Multi", "GRS451-AFR", "GRS451-EUR", "GRS451-Multi")
  }
  if (is.null(covariates)) {
    covariates <- c("None", "Age", "FHx", "Age + FHx")
  }

  include_age_only <- "Age" %in% predictors

  if (!is.null(outcome) & !is.null(metric)) {
     if (title) {
      print(paste0("Creating forest plot for outcome '", outcome, "' using metric '", metric, "'"))
    }
  } else {
    print("Warning: Please specify an outcome and metric to create the forest plot.")
  }

  if (!is.null(outcome) && !outcome %in% unique(data$Outcome)) {
    print(paste0("Warning: Outcome '", outcome, "' not found in the data. Please check the available outcomes. These are typically: 'PrCa_post_assessment', 'PrCa_2yrs', 'PrCa_5yrs', 'PrCa_10yrs'"))
  }

  if (!all(populations %in% unique(data$Population))) {
    unidentified_populations <- populations[!populations %in% unique(data$Population)]
    print(paste0("Warning: One or more populations not found in the data: ", paste(unidentified_populations, collapse = ", "), ". Please check the available populations. These are typically: 'White', 'Black', 'EUR', 'AFR'"))
  }

  if (!all(predictors %in% unique(data$Predictor))) {
    print(paste0("Warning: One or more predictors not found in the data. Please check the available predictors. These are typically: 'Age', 'GRS269-AFR', 'GRS269-EUR', 'GRS269-Multi', 'GRS451-AFR', 'GRS451-EUR', 'GRS451-Multi'"))
  }

  if (!all(covariates %in% unique(data$Covariates))) {
    print(paste0("Warning: One or more covariates not found in the data. Please check the available covariates. These are typically: 'None', 'Age', 'FHx', 'Age + FHx'"))
  }

  if (!is.null(metric) && !metric %in% c("ROC_AUC", "OR_per_1SD")) {
    print(paste0("Warning: Metric '", metric, "' not found in the data. Please check the available metrics. These are typically: 'ROC_AUC', 'OR_per_1SD'"))
  }

  base_forestplot <- data %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      Population %in% populations,
      Predictor %in% predictors,
      (Covariates %in% covariates) |
        (include_age_only & Predictor == "Age" & Covariates == "None"),
      Outcome == outcome
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Population = factor(Population, levels = rev(populations)),
      Model = dplyr::if_else(
        Covariates == "None",
        paste(Predictor, "only"),
        paste(Predictor, Covariates, sep = " + ")
      )
    ) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Covariate_Count = dplyr::if_else(
        Covariates == "None",
        0L,
        stringr::str_count(Covariates, "\\+") + 1L
      ),
      Model_Order = dplyr::case_when(
        Predictor == "Age" ~ 1,
        stringr::str_detect(Predictor, "GRS269-Multi|ContimultiethnicGRS267|ContiMultiethnicGRS") ~ 2,
        TRUE ~ 3
      )
    )

  model_levels <- base_forestplot %>%
    dplyr::distinct(Model, Predictor, Covariates, Model_Order, Covariate_Count) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(Model_Order, Predictor, Covariate_Count, Covariates) %>%
    dplyr::pull(Model)

  model_palette <- setNames(study_palette[seq_along(model_levels)], model_levels)

  forestplot <- base_forestplot %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      !is.na(.data[[metric]]),
      !is.na(.data[[paste0(metric, "_CI_Lower")]]),
      !is.na(.data[[paste0(metric, "_CI_Upper")]])
    ) %>%
    dplyr::arrange(Model_Order, Predictor, Covariate_Count, Covariates) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Model = factor(Model, levels = model_levels)
    )

  dodge_pos <- position_dodge(width = 0.6, reverse = TRUE)

  # Change plot limits here
  plot_limits <- if (metric == "ROC_AUC") {
      c(0.5, 1.0)
    } else if (metric == "OR_per_1SD") {
      c(1, 3)
    } else {
      NULL
    }

  outcome_label <- dplyr::case_when(
    outcome == "PrCa_2yrs" ~ "2-year",
    outcome == "PrCa_5yrs" ~ "5-year",
    outcome == "PrCa_10yrs" ~ "10-year",
    outcome == "PrCa_post_assessment" ~ "Post-assessment",
    TRUE ~ outcome
  )

  metric_label <- dplyr::case_when(
    metric == "ROC_AUC" ~ "ROC AUC",
    metric == "OR_per_1SD" ~ "OR per 1SD", # Only global OR per 1SD was calculated in the UK Biobank analyses
    TRUE ~ metric
  )

  metric_axis_label <- paste0(outcome_label, " ", metric_label, " [95% CI]")

  plot_obj <- ggplot(
    forestplot,
    aes(x = Population, y = .data[[metric]], color = Model)
  ) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = ifelse(metric == "ROC_AUC", 0.5, 1), linetype = "dashed", color = "#898b8d") +
    geom_errorbar(
      aes(ymin = .data[[paste0(metric, "_CI_Lower")]], ymax = .data[[paste0(metric, "_CI_Upper")]]),
      position = dodge_pos,
      width = 0.2,
      linewidth = 0.5
    ) +
    geom_point(
      position = dodge_pos,
      size = point_size
    ) +
    coord_flip(ylim = plot_limits) +
    labs(
      title = if (isTRUE(title)) {
        paste0(
          "Forest plot for outcome '",
          outcome,
          "'"
        )
      } else {
        NULL
      },
      x = "Population",
      y = metric_axis_label,
      color = "Model"
    ) +
    scale_color_manual(values = model_palette) +
    guides(color = guide_legend(reverse = FALSE)) +
    theme_minimal()

  if (!isTRUE(key)) {
    plot_obj <- plot_obj + theme(legend.position = "none")
  }

  return(plot_obj)
}
                               }


# Setup "plot_OR_table" function to convert Odds ratio tables (odds_ratio_summary) into a bar chart
#           x axis: model decile bin
#           y axis: odds ratio compared to 40th-60th percentile, recorded in "GRS alone", "Age", 
#                   "Age + GRS", "Age + FH", and "Age + GRS + FH" columns in summary tables 90 (white) and 91 (black). 
#                   In summary table 92, these columns are called "White men, GRS alone", "Black men, GRS alone", etc.,
#                   and bins are globally defined across both populations, rather than separately for each population.
#           Grouping factor: ethnicity group

plot_OR_table <- function(
    data = NULL,
    model = "Age + GRS",
    baseline_model = NULL,
    normalisation = "subpopulation",
    log_OR = FALSE,
    log_CI_floor = NULL,
    bin_column = NULL,
    populations = c("White", "Black"),
    title = TRUE,
    key = TRUE,
    bar_width = 0.75,
    errorbar_width = 0.20,
    y_limits = NULL,
    colours = c(
      "White" = "#00c896",
      "Black" = "#9569be"
    )
) {

  ## Check function inputs

  if (is.null(data)) {
    stop(
      paste0(
        "Error: Please provide either a data frame or a named list ",
        "of data frames for the 'data' argument."
      )
    )
  }

  valid_models <- c(
    "Age",
    "GRS alone",
    "Age + GRS",
    "Age + FH",
    "Age + GRS + FH"
  )

  if (!model %in% valid_models) {
    stop(
      paste0(
        "Error: model must be one of: ",
        paste(sprintf("'%s'", valid_models), collapse = ", "),
        "."
      )
    )
  }

  if (!is.null(baseline_model)) {

    if (!is.character(baseline_model) ||
        length(baseline_model) != 1 ||
        is.na(baseline_model) ||
        baseline_model == "") {
      stop(
        paste0(
          "Error: baseline_model must be NULL or a single ",
          "non-missing character value."
        )
      )
    }

    if (!baseline_model %in% valid_models) {
      stop(
        paste0(
          "Error: baseline_model must be NULL or one of: ",
          paste(sprintf("'%s'", valid_models), collapse = ", "),
          "."
        )
      )
    }

    if (baseline_model == model) {
      stop(
        "Error: baseline_model and model must refer to different models."
      )
    }
  }

  # Models are deliberately ordered with the baseline model first.
  selected_models <- if (is.null(baseline_model)) {
    model
  } else {
    c(baseline_model, model)
  }

  if (!normalisation %in% c("subpopulation", "global")) {
    stop(
      paste0(
        "Error: normalisation must be either ",
        "'subpopulation' or 'global'."
      )
    )
  }

  if (!is.numeric(bar_width) ||
      length(bar_width) != 1 ||
      is.na(bar_width) ||
      bar_width <= 0) {
    stop("Error: bar_width must be a single positive number.")
  }

  if (!is.numeric(errorbar_width) ||
      length(errorbar_width) != 1 ||
      is.na(errorbar_width) ||
      errorbar_width < 0) {
    stop("Error: errorbar_width must be a single non-negative number.")
  }

  if (!is.logical(log_OR) ||
      length(log_OR) != 1 ||
      is.na(log_OR)) {
    stop("Error: log_OR must be a single logical value (TRUE or FALSE).")
  }

  if (!is.null(log_CI_floor)) {
    if (!is.numeric(log_CI_floor) ||
        length(log_CI_floor) != 1 ||
        is.na(log_CI_floor) ||
        !is.finite(log_CI_floor) ||
        log_CI_floor <= 0) {
      stop(
        paste0(
          "Error: log_CI_floor must be NULL or a single finite ",
          "number greater than zero."
        )
      )
    }
  }



  ## Helper for identifying likely column names

  find_column <- function(data_names, candidates, argument_name) {

    matched_column <- candidates[candidates %in% data_names]

    if (length(matched_column) == 0) {
      stop(
        paste0(
          "Error: Could not identify the ", argument_name, " column. ",
          "Please specify it explicitly using the '",
          argument_name,
          "' argument. Available columns are: ",
          paste(data_names, collapse = ", "),
          "."
        )
      )
    }

    matched_column[[1]]
  }

  ## Prepare subpopulation-normalised data

  if (normalisation == "subpopulation") {

    # Subpopulation-normalised results are stored in two tables:
    #
    # summary_table_90 = White men
    # summary_table_91 = Black men
    #
    # Because the individual tables do not contain a population column,
    # the population is inferred from the supplied list-element name.

    if (!is.list(data) || is.data.frame(data)) {
      stop(
        paste0(
          "Error: For subpopulation normalisation, 'data' must be a list ",
          "containing summary_table_90 and/or summary_table_91. For example: ",
          "data = list(summary_table_90 = summary_table_90, ",
          "summary_table_91 = summary_table_91)."
        )
      )
    }

    if (!all(vapply(data, is.data.frame, logical(1)))) {
      stop(
        "Error: Every element supplied in 'data' must be a data frame."
      )
    }

    if (is.null(names(data)) ||
        any(is.na(names(data))) ||
        any(names(data) == "")) {
      stop(
        paste0(
          "Error: The supplied list must have named elements. Use: ",
          "list(summary_table_90 = summary_table_90, ",
          "summary_table_91 = summary_table_91)."
        )
      )
    }

    # Map each known summary table to its corresponding population.
    table_population_lookup <- c(
      "summary_table_90" = "White",
      "summary_table_91" = "Black"
    )

    unrecognised_tables <- setdiff(
      names(data),
      names(table_population_lookup)
    )

    if (length(unrecognised_tables) > 0) {
      stop(
        paste0(
          "Error: The following table names were not recognised: ",
          paste(unrecognised_tables, collapse = ", "),
          ". Expected list-element names are 'summary_table_90' ",
          "and/or 'summary_table_91'."
        )
      )
    }

    ## Check that all selected model columns occur in every supplied table

    missing_model_columns_by_table <- lapply(
      data,
      function(current_table) {
        setdiff(selected_models, names(current_table))
      }
    )

    tables_missing_models <- names(
      missing_model_columns_by_table
    )[
      lengths(missing_model_columns_by_table) > 0
    ]

    if (length(tables_missing_models) > 0) {

      missing_model_message <- vapply(
        tables_missing_models,
        function(table_name) {
          paste0(
            table_name,
            ": ",
            paste(
              missing_model_columns_by_table[[table_name]],
              collapse = ", "
            )
          )
        },
        character(1)
      )

      stop(
        paste0(
          "Error: The following model columns were not found: ",
          paste(missing_model_message, collapse = "; "),
          "."
        )
      )
    }


    # Add population and reshape the selected models into long format.
    prepared_tables <- lapply(
      names(data),
      function(table_name) {

        current_table <- data[[table_name]]

        current_table %>%
          dplyr::mutate(
            Population = unname(
              table_population_lookup[[table_name]]
            )
          ) %>%
          tidyr::pivot_longer(
            cols = dplyr::all_of(selected_models),
            names_to = "Plotted_Model",
            values_to = "OR_string"
          ) %>%
          dplyr::mutate(
            OR_string = as.character(OR_string)
          )
      }
    )

    plot_data <- dplyr::bind_rows(prepared_tables)
  }

  ## Prepare globally normalised data

  if (normalisation == "global") {

    if (!is.data.frame(data)) {
      stop(
        paste0(
          "Error: For global normalisation, 'data' must be the ",
          "globally normalised summary data frame."
        )
      )
    }

    ## Create a lookup between source columns, populations and models

    global_column_lookup <- tidyr::expand_grid(
      Population = populations,
      Plotted_Model = selected_models
    ) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        Source_Column = paste0(
          Population,
          " men, ",
          Plotted_Model
        )
      )

    global_model_columns <- global_column_lookup$Source_Column

    missing_model_columns <- setdiff(
      global_model_columns,
      names(data)
    )

    if (length(missing_model_columns) > 0) {
      stop(
        paste0(
          "Error: The following globally normalised model columns ",
          "were not found: ",
          paste(missing_model_columns, collapse = ", "),
          "."
        )
      )
    }

    plot_data <- data %>%
      tidyr::pivot_longer(
        cols = dplyr::all_of(global_model_columns),
        names_to = "Source_Column",
        values_to = "OR_string"
      ) %>%
      dplyr::left_join(
        global_column_lookup,
        by = "Source_Column"
      ) %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        OR_string = as.character(OR_string)
      )
  }

  ## Identify the decile-bin column

  if (is.null(bin_column)) {

    bin_column_internal <- find_column(
      data_names = names(plot_data),
      candidates = c(
        "Model decile bin",
        "Model_Decile_Bin",
        "Model_decile_bin",
        "Decile bin",
        "Decile_Bin",
        "Decile",
        "decile",
        "Bin",
        "bin",
        "Percentile bin",
        "Percentile_Bin",
        "Percentile"
      ),
      argument_name = "bin_column"
    )

  } else {

    if (!bin_column %in% names(plot_data)) {
      stop(
        paste0(
          "Error: bin_column '",
          bin_column,
          "' was not found in the supplied data."
        )
      )
    }

    bin_column_internal <- bin_column
  }

  ## Parse the formatted OR strings

  # Expected general format:
  # 1.23 [1.10, 1.38]; p=1.45e-06
  #
  # Spaces around commas, brackets, semicolons and "=" signs are
  # permitted. The p-value may also be written as p<...

  plot_data <- plot_data %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Model_Bin = as.character(.data[[bin_column_internal]]),

      # Convert labels such as "0-10th percentile" to "0-10%".
      Model_Bin = stringr::str_replace(
        Model_Bin,
        stringr::regex(
          paste0(
            "^\\s*([0-9.]+)\\s*[-–]\\s*([0-9.]+)",
            "(?:st|nd|rd|th)?\\s*percentile\\s*$"
          ),
          ignore_case = TRUE
          ),
        "\\1-\\2%"
      ),
      OR_string = as.character(OR_string),

      OR_mean = as.numeric(
        stringr::str_extract(
          OR_string,
          "^[[:space:]]*[0-9]*\\.?[0-9]+(?:[eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?"
        )
      ),

      OR_CI_lower = as.numeric(
        stringr::str_match(
          OR_string,
          "\\[[[:space:]]*([0-9]*\\.?[0-9]+(?:[eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?)"
        )[, 2]
      ),

      OR_CI_upper = as.numeric(
        stringr::str_match(
          OR_string,
          ",[[:space:]]*([0-9]*\\.?[0-9]+(?:[eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?)[[:space:]]*\\]"
        )[, 2]
      ),

      OR_p_value = as.numeric(
        stringr::str_match(
          OR_string,
          "[pP][[:space:]]*[=<][[:space:]]*([0-9]*\\.?[0-9]+(?:[eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?)"
        )[, 2]
      )
    )

  ## Restrict and order populations

  missing_populations <- setdiff(
    populations,
    unique(plot_data$Population)
  )

  if (length(missing_populations) > 0) {
    warning(
      paste0(
        "The following requested populations were not found and will ",
        "not be plotted: ",
        paste(missing_populations, collapse = ", "),
        "."
      ),
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  plot_data <- plot_data %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      Population %in% populations
    )

  if (nrow(plot_data) == 0) {
    stop(
      "Error: No rows remain after filtering to the requested populations."
    )
  }

  ## Check whether OR values were parsed successfully

  failed_parsing <- plot_data %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      !is.na(OR_string),
      OR_string != "",
      is.na(OR_mean) |
        is.na(OR_CI_lower) |
        is.na(OR_CI_upper)
    )

  if (nrow(failed_parsing) > 0) {
    warning(
      paste0(
        nrow(failed_parsing),
        " row(s) contained OR strings that could not be fully parsed. ",
        "These rows will be excluded from the plot."
      ),
      call. = FALSE
    )
  }

  plot_data <- plot_data %>%
    dplyr::filter(
      !is.na(OR_mean),
      !is.na(OR_CI_lower),
      !is.na(OR_CI_upper)
    )

  if (nrow(plot_data) == 0) {
    stop(
      paste0(
        "Error: No rows with successfully parsed OR and 95% CI values ",
        "remain for plotting."
      )
    )
  }

  ## Prepare y-axis values

  if (isTRUE(log_OR)) {

    # The OR estimate and upper confidence limit must be strictly positive.
    invalid_log_values <- plot_data %>%
      dplyr::filter(
        OR_mean <= 0 |
          OR_CI_upper <= 0 |
          OR_CI_lower < 0
      )

    if (nrow(invalid_log_values) > 0) {
      stop(
        paste0(
          "Error: log_OR = TRUE requires OR estimates and upper ",
          "confidence limits to be greater than zero, and lower ",
          "confidence limits to be non-negative. ",
          nrow(invalid_log_values),
          " row(s) contained invalid values."
        )
      )
    }

    # Identify lower confidence limits that were recorded as zero.
    zero_lower_CI <- plot_data$OR_CI_lower == 0

    if (any(zero_lower_CI)) {

      if (is.null(log_CI_floor)) {

        positive_lower_CIs <- plot_data$OR_CI_lower[
          is.finite(plot_data$OR_CI_lower) &
            plot_data$OR_CI_lower > 0
        ]

        if (length(positive_lower_CIs) > 0) {

          # Use one-tenth of the smallest observed positive lower CI.
          effective_log_CI_floor <- min(positive_lower_CIs) / 10

        } else {

          # Fallback if every lower confidence limit is zero.
          effective_log_CI_floor <- 0.001
        }

      } else {
        
        effective_log_CI_floor <- log_CI_floor
      }

      warning(
        paste0(
          sum(zero_lower_CI),
          " lower confidence limit(s) were recorded as 0.00 and ",
          "cannot be represented on a log scale. For plotting only, ",
          "these values have been set to ",
          format(effective_log_CI_floor, scientific = TRUE),
          ". The displayed y-axis has been truncated above this ",
          "arbitrary floor, and downward triangles identify affected ",
          "confidence intervals. The original OR_CI_lower values ",
          "remain unchanged."
        ),
        call. = FALSE
      )

    } else {

        # No replacement used, this is just a numeric value for the subsequent if_else() call
        effective_log_CI_floor <- 1
    }

    plot_data <- plot_data %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        Lower_CI_Truncated = OR_CI_lower == 0,

        # Create a separate plotting value so OR_CI_lower is preserved.
        OR_CI_lower_plot = dplyr::if_else(
          Lower_CI_Truncated,
          effective_log_CI_floor,
          OR_CI_lower
        ),

        y_mean = log(OR_mean),
        y_lower = log(OR_CI_lower_plot),
        y_upper = log(OR_CI_upper)
      )

    reference_value <- 0
    y_axis_label <- "log(Odds ratio) [95% CI]"

  } else {

    plot_data <- plot_data %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        Lower_CI_Truncated = FALSE,
        OR_CI_lower_plot = OR_CI_lower,
        y_mean = OR_mean,
        y_lower = OR_CI_lower,
        y_upper = OR_CI_upper
      )

    reference_value <- 1
    y_axis_label <- "Odds ratio [95% CI]"
  }

  ## Preserve the original bin order

  bin_levels <- unique(plot_data$Model_Bin)

  # Explicitly define the order of populations and models.
  #
  # Bar ordering within each percentile bin will be:
  #   Population 1, baseline
  #   Population 1, primary model
  #   Population 2, baseline
  #   Population 2, primary model


  bar_group_levels <- unlist(
    lapply(
      populations,
      function(current_population) {
        paste(
          current_population,
          selected_models,
          sep = "|||"
        )
      }
    ),
    use.names = FALSE
  )

  plot_data <- plot_data %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Model_Bin = factor(
        Model_Bin,
        levels = bin_levels
      ),
      Population = factor(
        Population,
        levels = populations
      ),
      Plotted_Model = factor(
        Plotted_Model,
        levels = selected_models
      ),
      Bar_Group = factor(
        paste(
          as.character(Population),
          as.character(Plotted_Model),
          sep = "|||"
        ),
        levels = bar_group_levels
      )
    )

  ## Set population colours

  if (is.null(names(colours))) {
    if (length(colours) < length(populations)) {
      stop(
        "Error: The unnamed colours vector is shorter than populations."
      )
    }

    colours <- stats::setNames(
      colours[seq_along(populations)],
      populations
    )
  }

  missing_colours <- setdiff(
    populations,
    names(colours)
  )

  if (length(missing_colours) > 0) {
    stop(
      paste0(
        "Error: No colour has been supplied for: ",
        paste(missing_colours, collapse = ", "),
        "."
      )
    )
  }

  ## Set plot fill groups and co*ours

  if (is.null(baseline_model)) {

    # With one model, retain *he original population-only legend*
    plot_data <- plot_data %>%
     dplyr::mutate(
        Plot_Fill_Group = factor(
          as.character(Population),
          levels = populations
        )
      )

    plot_fill_colours <- colours[populations]
    fill_legend_title <- "Population"

  } else {

    # Create ordered composite legend labels
    composite_legend_labels <- unlist(
      lapply(
        populations,
        function(current_population) {
          paste0(
            current_population,
            " men, ",
            selected_models
          )
        }
      ),
      use.names = FALSE
    )

    plot_data <- plot_data %>%
      dplyr::mutate(
        Plot_Fill_Group = factor(
          paste0(
            as.character(Population),
            " men, ",
            as.character(Plotted_Model)
          ),
          levels = composite_legend_labels
        )
      )

    # Baseline colours use the population colour at reduced opacity.
    # Primary-model colours use the fully opaque population colour.
    plot_fill_colours <- unlist(
      lapply(
        populations,
        function(current_population) {

          stats::setNames(
            c(
              grDevices::adjustcolor(
                colours[[current_population]],
                alpha.f = 0.55
              ),
              colours[[current_population]]
            ),
            paste0(
              current_population,
              " men, ",
              selected_models
            )
          )
        }
      ),
      use.names = TRUE
    )

    fill_legend_title <- "Population and model"
  }

  ## Construct plot labels

  normalisation_label <- dplyr::case_when(
    normalisation == "subpopulation" ~ "Subpopulation-normalised",
    normalisation == "global" ~ "Globally normalised",
    TRUE ~ normalisation
  )

  x_axis_label <- dplyr::case_when(
    normalisation == "subpopulation" ~
      "Model percentile bin (subpopulation-standardised)",
    normalisation == "global" ~
      "Model percentile bin (globally-standardised)",
    TRUE ~ "Model percentile bin"
  )

  plot_model_label <- if (is.null(baseline_model)) {
    model
  } else {
    paste0(
      baseline_model,
      " versus ",
      model
    )
  }

  plot_title <- if (isTRUE(title)) {
    paste0(
      plot_model_label,
      ": ",
      normalisation_label,
      " model bins"
    )
  } else {
    NULL
  }

  ## Determine displayed y-axis limits

  if (is.null(y_limits)) {

    if (isTRUE(log_OR)) {

      observed_y_max <- max(
        plot_data$y_upper,
        plot_data$y_mean,
        reference_value,
        na.rm = TRUE
      )

      if (any(plot_data$Lower_CI_Truncated)) {

        # Exclude arbitrary plotting-floor values when determining
        # the lower visible y-axis boundary.
        empirical_y_lower <- plot_data$y_lower[
          !plot_data$Lower_CI_Truncated &
            is.finite(plot_data$y_lower)
        ]

        if (length(empirical_y_lower) > 0) {

          # The next-lowest CI is the lowest non-truncated lower CI.
          observed_y_min <- min(
            empirical_y_lower,
            plot_data$y_mean,
            reference_value,
            na.rm = TRUE
          )

        } else {

          # Fallback if every lower confidence limit was truncated.
          # In this situation, use the lowest point estimate.
          observed_y_min <- min(
            plot_data$y_mean,
            reference_value,
            na.rm = TRUE
          )

          warning(
            paste0(
              "Every lower confidence limit was truncated. The lower ",
              "displayed y-axis boundary has therefore been based on ",
              "the lowest point estimate rather than a non-truncated ",
              "lower confidence limit."
            ),
            call. = FALSE
          )
        }

      } else {

        # No arbitrary floor was used, so include all lower CIs.
        observed_y_min <- min(
          plot_data$y_lower,
          plot_data$y_mean,
          reference_value,
          na.rm = TRUE
        )
      }

      y_range <- observed_y_max - observed_y_min

      # Protect against a zero-height or non-finite range.
      if (!is.finite(y_range) || y_range == 0) {
        y_range <- 1
      }

      effective_y_limits <- c(
        observed_y_min - 0.03 * y_range,
        observed_y_max + 0.05 * y_range
      )

    } else {

      # For the untransformed OR plot, force the lower boundary to zero.
      observed_y_max <- max(
        plot_data$y_upper,
        plot_data$y_mean,
        reference_value,
        na.rm = TRUE
      )

      effective_y_limits <- c(
        0,
        observed_y_max * 1.05
      )
    }

  } else {

    if (!is.numeric(y_limits) ||
        length(y_limits) != 2 ||
        anyNA(y_limits) ||
        !all(is.finite(y_limits)) ||
        y_limits[[1]] >= y_limits[[2]]) {
      stop(
        paste0(
          "Error: y_limits must be NULL or an increasing numeric ",
          "vector of two finite values."
        )
      )
    }

    effective_y_limits <- y_limits
  }

  ## Set marker position for truncated confidence intervals

  displayed_y_range <- diff(effective_y_limits)

  plot_data <- plot_data %>%
    dplyr::mutate(
      Truncation_Marker_Y = dplyr::if_else(
        Lower_CI_Truncated,
        effective_y_limits[[1]] + 0.02 * displayed_y_range,
        NA_real_
      )
    )

  ## Create grouped bar chart

  dodge_position <- ggplot2::position_dodge(
    width = bar_width,
    preserve = "single"
  )

  plot_obj <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    plot_data,
    ggplot2::aes(
      x = Model_Bin,
      y = y_mean,
      fill = Plot_Fill_Group,
      group = Bar_Group
    )
  ) +
    ggplot2::geom_hline(
      yintercept = reference_value,
      linetype = "dashed",
      colour = "#898b8d",
      linewidth = 0.5
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_col(
      position = dodge_position,
      width = bar_width,
      colour = "black",
      linewidth = 0.25
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_errorbar(
      ggplot2::aes(
        ymin = y_lower,
        ymax = y_upper
      ),
      position = dodge_position,
      width = errorbar_width,
      linewidth = 0.5
    ) +
    ggplot2::geom_point(
      ggplot2::aes(
        y = Truncation_Marker_Y
      ),
      position = dodge_position,
      shape = 25,
      size = 2.5,
      colour = "black",
      inherit.aes = TRUE,
      show.legend = FALSE,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(
      values = plot_fill_colours,
      drop = FALSE
    ) +
    ggplot2::labs(
      title = plot_title,
      x = x_axis_label,
      y = y_axis_label,
      fill = fill_legend_title
    ) +
    ggplot2::theme_minimal() +
    ggplot2::theme(
      panel.grid.major.x = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor = ggplot2::element_blank(),
      axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(
        angle = 45,
        hjust = 1
      )
    )

    # coord_cartesian avoids dropping bars or error bars that extend
    # beyond the displayed range.
    plot_obj <- plot_obj +
      ggplot2::coord_cartesian(
        ylim = effective_y_limits,
        clip = "on"
      )

  if (!isTRUE(key)) {
    plot_obj <- plot_obj +
      ggplot2::theme(
        legend.position = "none"
      )
  }
  

  return(plot_obj)

}

## P value formatting functions
format_p_value <- function(p, zero_p_upper_bound = 5e-8, ...) {
  if (length(p) != 1 || is.na(p)) {
    return(NA_character_)
  }

  # A value stored as zero after rounding to seven decimal places is a
  # reporting limit, not an exact p value.
  if (p == 0) {
    scientific_bound <- formatC(
      zero_p_upper_bound,
      format = "e",
      digits = 2
    )

    return(paste0("&lt; ", scientific_bound))
  }

  if (p < 0.01) {
    formatC(p, format = "e", digits = 2)
  } else {
    formatC(p, format = "f", digits = 2)
  }
}

round <- function(x, digits = 0, ...) {
  expression_text <- paste(deparse(substitute(x)), collapse = "")

  if (
    grepl("p_value_BH", expression_text, fixed = TRUE) ||
    grepl("OR_p_value", expression_text, fixed = TRUE) ||
    grepl("p_value", expression_text, fixed = TRUE)
  ) {
    return(format_p_value(x))
  }

  formatC(
    x,
    format = "f",
    digits = digits
  )
}
```

```{r extra_variables_for_paper_text, eval=TRUE, echo=FALSE, include=FALSE, cache=FALSE}
## Did ROC AUC values increase or decrease with longer prediction horizons in UKB?

ukb_roc_auc_pattern_summary <- asymptomatic_screening_summary %>%
  dplyr::filter(
    Outcome %in% c("PrCa_2yrs", "PrCa_5yrs", "PrCa_10yrs"),
    Population %in% c("White", "Black", "EUR", "AFR"),
    !is.na(ROC_AUC)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(Population, Predictor, Covariates) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    ROC_AUC_2yrs = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(first(ROC_AUC[Outcome == "PrCa_2yrs"]))),
    ROC_AUC_5yrs = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(first(ROC_AUC[Outcome == "PrCa_5yrs"]))),
    ROC_AUC_10yrs = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(first(ROC_AUC[Outcome == "PrCa_10yrs"]))),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    all_outcomes_present = !is.na(ROC_AUC_2yrs) & !is.na(ROC_AUC_5yrs) & !is.na(ROC_AUC_10yrs),
    pattern_2yr_gt_5yr_gt_10yr = all_outcomes_present & (ROC_AUC_2yrs > ROC_AUC_5yrs) & (ROC_AUC_5yrs > ROC_AUC_10yrs)
  )

ukb_pct_2yr_gt_5yr_gt_10yr <- ukb_roc_auc_pattern_summary %>%
  dplyr::filter(all_outcomes_present) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(pct = mean(pattern_2yr_gt_5yr_gt_10yr) * 100) %>%
  dplyr::pull(pct)

if (length(ukb_pct_2yr_gt_5yr_gt_10yr) == 0 || is.na(ukb_pct_2yr_gt_5yr_gt_10yr)) {
  ukb_roc_auc_increased_or_decreased_with_longer_prediction_horizons <- NA_character_

} else {
  ukb_roc_auc_increased_or_decreased_with_longer_prediction_horizons <- "decreased"
}
```
